latest_release.name: v0.2.2
latest_release.body:
### Added

- AOF rewrite on a background thread: `BGREWRITEAOF` and automatic rewrites (`auto-aof-rewrite-percentage`, `auto-aof-rewrite-min-size`) replace the AOF with a snapshot of the live dataset, so it no longer grows without bound, and the server keeps serving while it runs. The store has no locks, so the rewrite thread never touches it: it replays the existing AOF into a private store (what a restart would load), writes strings (with TTLs), lists and time series as commands to a temp file, copies the log written meanwhile, and the writer thread splices on the last bytes, fsyncs, and atomically renames it into place. On 400k keys it took about 0.5 s with `PING` latency unchanged. It needs memory for a second copy of the dataset while it runs, outside `maxmemory`; because evictions are not logged to the AOF, that copy can also hold keys the live store has evicted (as a restart would). It is refused, leaving the AOF untouched, while the dataset holds bloom filters or search indexes, which commands cannot recreate. `INFO` reports `aof_rewrite_in_progress`, `aof_rewrites`, `aof_last_rewrite_time` and `aof_last_bgrewrite_status`; `METRICS` reports `zedis_aof_rewrites_total`.

- Real observability: `INFO` now reports live command, connection, keyspace
  hit/miss, expiry, eviction, network, memory, CPU, and AOF counters; new
  `INFO commandstats`; `SLOWLOG GET|LEN|RESET`; `LATENCY LATEST|HISTORY|RESET|DOCTOR`;
  and `METRICS` for Prometheus text scraping.
- `slowlog-log-slower-than`, `slowlog-max-len`, `latency-monitor-threshold`,
  and `command-timeout-ms` config keys, all mutable with `CONFIG SET`.
- Graceful shutdown on `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` and `SHUTDOWN [NOSAVE|SAVE]`. The
  accept loops stop, clients are woken, and the AOF writer drains and fsyncs
  before the process exits.
- `CONFIG REWRITE` persists mutable directives to the config file using an
  atomic temp-file rename, preserving comments and unrelated lines.
- Read-only `O(N)` commands (`KEYS`, `SCAN`, `LRANGE`) accept a cooperative
  deadline and reply `-TIMEOUT` instead of stalling without bound. `SCAN`
  remains the `KEYS` replacement; the timeout bounds a stall rather than
  removing it.
- TLS listener via OpenSSL: `tls-port`, `tls-cert-file`, `tls-key-file`, `tls-ca-cert-file`, `tls-auth-clients` (`yes`/`no`/`optional`) and `tls-protocols`. TLS can run alongside plaintext or replace it with `port 0`; mutual TLS verifies client certificates against the configured CA. OpenSSL is linked statically by default.
- RESP3 support, negotiated per connection with `HELLO [2|3] [AUTH default <password>] [SETNAME name]`. Connections stay on RESP2 until a client sends `HELLO 3`. Under RESP3, missing values reply with the null type (`_`), floats with the double type (`,`), and `CONFIG GET` and `BF.INFO` with a map (`%`). Pub/sub deliveries and `SUBSCRIBE`/`UNSUBSCRIBE` replies are push messages (`>`), while RESP2 subscribers on the same channel keep receiving arrays.

### Changed

- Startup no longer carries on after a failed AOF load. A damaged or unreplayable AOF now stops the server with an error instead of serving a partial dataset and appending to the bad file. `aof-load-truncated` (default `yes`) lets it cut off a final command left half-written by a crash, and `aof-load-broken` with `aof-load-broken-max-size` lets it discard a small corrupt tail; the cut is applied to the file so later writes append to a valid log. Any other corruption, or a command this build does not know, still stops startup.
- The AOF is now loaded before its writer opens, since the writer begins appending at the file's length.

### Fixed

- A float reply longer than 32 characters (for example a time-series sample of `1e300`) overflowed a fixed buffer: a panic in safe builds, truncated output in `ReleaseFast`.

---

## Install

**Linux (x86_64)**
```bash
curl -Lo zedis https://github.com/charlesfonseca/zedis/releases/download/v0.2.2/zedis-v0.2.2-linux-x86_64
chmod +x zedis && sudo mv zedis /usr/loca

detail.readme: # Zedis [![Release](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/actions/workflows/release.yml) A Redis-compatible in-memory data store written in [Zig](https://ziglang.org/), designed for learning and experimentation. Zedis implements the core Redis protocol and data structures with a focus on simplicity, performance, and thread safety. ## Features - **Redis Protocol Compatibility**: Supports the Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP), including pipelined commands. - **Multiple Data Types**: Strings and integers, lists, time series, and Bloom filters. - **Core Commands**: Key management (`DEL`, `EXISTS`, `TYPE`, `TTL`, `EXPIRE`, `KEYS`), strings, lists (`LPUSH`/`RPUSH`/`LRANGE`, ...), and `RANDOMKEY`. - **High Performance**: Written in Zig, with a single-executor command path and no global store lock. - **Key Expiration**: Lazy TTL expiry on access, plus expiry checks during eviction. - **Disk persistence (RDB)**: Point-in-time snapshots of your dataset. - **Append-only file (AOF)**: Durable write-ahead logging with group commit. - **Memory Budgeting**: Redis-compatible `maxmemory` with eviction, `-OOM` rejection for allocating commands, and cgroup-aware auto-sizing inside containers. - **Pub/Sub**: Decoupled communication between services, with push delivery to idle subscribers. - **TLS**: Optional TLS 1.2/1.3 listener (OpenSSL) with certificate/key/CA configuration and optional mutual TLS via `tls-auth-clients`. - **Observability**: Real `INFO` counters (connections, ops/sec, hit rate, memory, AOF state), `SLOWLOG`, `LATENCY`, and a `METRICS` command exposing Prometheus text exposition. - **Graceful shutdown**: `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` and `SHUTDOWN [NOSAVE|SAVE]` stop accepting, drain clients, flush the AOF, and close the listeners. `CONFIG REWRITE` persists runtime changes. - **Time Series**: Time series data structure. **Now with Gorilla compression!** - **Opinionated Design**: No multiple logical databases, expiry is lazy only. ## Caveats - Zedis is intentionally single-store. It does not support multiple logical databases and does not expose Redis `SELECT`. It adds complexity and segment memory. This follows the reasoning Salvatore Sanfilippo gave when he called Redis multiple databases one of [his worst design decisions](https://groups.google.com/g/redis-db/c/vS5wX8X4Cjg/m/8ounBXitG4sJ). ## Quick Start Download the binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/releases) or build from source to get started with Zedis. ### Prerequisites - [Zig](https://ziglang.org/download/) 0.17.1 (pinned in `build.zig.zon`) ### Building and Running ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/barddoo/zedis.git cd zedis # Build the project (optimized, ReleaseFast) zig build --release=fast # Run the server zig build run --release=fast ``` The server will start on `127.0.0.1:6379` by default. ### Testing with Redis CLI You can test Zedis using the standard `redis-cli` or any Redis client: ```bash # Connect to Zedis redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6379 # Try some commands 127.0.0.1:6379> SET mykey "Hello, Zedis!" OK 127.0.0.1:6379> GET mykey "Hello, Zedis!" 127.0.0.1:6379> INCR counter (integer) 1 127.0.0.1:6379> TYPE mykey string ``` ### TLS Enable the TLS listener in the config file (see `zedis.conf` for all options): ```conf port 0 # optional: serve TLS only tls-port 6380 tls-cert-file /etc/zedis/server.crt tls-key-file /etc/zedis/server.key tls-ca-cert-file /etc/zedis/ca.crt tls-auth-clients no # yes (default), no, or optional ``` Then connect with any TLS-capable Redis client, for example: ```bash redis-cli --tls --insecure -p 6380 ``` ## Docker Pre-built images are available on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/barddoo/zedis): ```bash docker run -p 6379:6379 barddoo/zedis ``` ### Variants | Tag | Base | Notes | Use case | | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------- | -------------------------- | | `latest`, `x.x.x`, `x.x.x-debian`, `x.x.x-slim` | Debian Trixie slim | Larger, glibc base | Default; broader ecosystem | | `x.x.x-alpine`, `alpine` | Alpine 3.20 | Smallest with shell | Size-sensitive deployments | | `x.x.x-distroless` | Distroless static | No shell | Security-sensitive | ### Persistent data Mount a volume to persist data across restarts: ```bash docker run -p 6379:6379 -v zedis-data:/var/lib/zedis/data barddoo/zedis ``` ### Custom config ```bash docker run -p 6379:6379 -v ./zedis.conf:/etc/zedis/zedis.conf barddoo/zedis ``` ## Development ### Project Structure The codebase is split by responsibility: - `src/app/` — server lifecycle, client connections, config, clock - `src/storage/` — store, KV allocator, lists, time series, Bloom filters, search - `src/commands/` — command handlers and registry - `src/persistence/` — AOF and RDB - `src/protocol/` — RESP parser and serializer - `src/util/` — mailbox, stack writer, types, compression - `src/benchmarks/` — micro/load benchmarks See `docs/server-architecture.md` for the current server thread model and request flow. ### Memory Management See `docs/memory-architecture.md` for the current allocator layout, memory budgets, and runtime allocation behavior. See `docs/store-cache-layout.md` for the store's hash-table layout and cache behavior. ### Building for Development TLS support links OpenSSL. On macOS install it with `brew install openssl@4` (the build auto-detects the Homebrew keg); on Debian/Ubuntu install `libssl-dev`, and on Alpine install `openssl-dev openssl-libs-static`. OpenSSL is linked statically by default; pass `-Dopenssl-static=false` for a dynamic link, or `-Dopenssl-prefix=/path` for a non-standard prefix. ```bash # Build in debug mode (default) zig build # Build optimized release (ReleaseFast; use this for benchmarks and performance testing) zig build --release=fast # `--release` with no mode also picks ReleaseFast (the preferred mode in build.zig) zig build --release # Run the full test suite zig build test # Run a focused subset zig build test -Dtest-filter="Store" # Format the source zig fmt . ``` ## AI Disclaimer This project was developed with some AI help. Most of the code was written by hand. ## Contributing Contributors are welcome! Whether you're fixing bugs, adding features, improving documentation, or suggesting enhancements, your contributions are appreciated. Feel free to: - Open an issue to report bugs or suggest features - Submit pull requests with improvements - Share feedback and ideas Check out the [open issues](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/issues) to see where you can help. ## Stay Connected - Subscribe to my [newsletter](https://charlesfonseca.substack.com) ## Thanks - [Andrew Kelley](https://andrewkelley.me) - For creating the amazing [Zig Language](https://ziglang.org/). - [Redis](https://redis.io/) - For the inspiration and protocol design. - [TigerBeetle](https://tigerbeetle.com/) - For the memory management and the tiger style. - [Karl Seguin](https://github.com/karlseguin) - For the great articles.
